from sort import sort_list

{"content": "AUDIT OF AXIOMS, ASSUMPTIONS, AND DEPENDENCIES
==============================================

Scope:   sort.py, logic.txt, obligations.txt, proof.txt, checker.py
Method:  Each item is classified (AXIOM / DEFINITION / TRUST /
         EMPIRICAL), assessed, and given a verdict. References are to
         the sections of logic.txt, proof.txt, obligations.txt.

Classification key:
    AXIOM      Assumed without proof; unrecoverable if false.
    DERIVED    Justified inside the development (proved or checked).
    TRUST      Outside the checker kernel; accepted on audit/review.
    EMPIRICAL  Supported by testing only; not a proof.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
A. LOGICAL FRAMEWORK
------------------------------------------------------------------------
[A1] First-order logic with equality, two-sorted (Z, List), natural
     deduction rules (logic.txt 2; proof.txt 1 rule set, enforced by
     checker.py).
     Status: AXIOM (framework).
     Assessment: Standard and minimal. Soundness of FOL is a
     meta-theorem with a century of scrutiny; the checker re-checks
     every rule instance syntactically, so only the rule *schemas* are
     trusted, not any particular inference.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE.

[A2] List induction schema L3 (logic.txt 2.2): from P(nil) and
     forall x xs. P(xs) -> P(cons(x, xs)) infer forall L. P(L).
     Status: AXIOM.
     Assessment: Valid for the free term algebra nil/cons with
     finite lists only. All uses in proof.txt (steps 1.10, 2.8, 4.8,
     6.8, 6.11, 8.6, 8.10, 9.3, 9.6) induct over List-typed variables
     constructed by cons from nil; no coinductive or infinite lists
     are involved. Sound for the intended model of Python lists as
     finite sequences.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE.

[A3] Integer arithmetic axioms A1-A6 (logic.txt 2.1): irreflexivity,
     transitivity, trichotomy of <, discreteness (x < y <-> x+1 <= y),
     associativity/commutativity/unit of +, and the <= expansion.
     Status: AXIOM.
     Assessment: These hold in Z with the standard order and addition,
     which is the intended model of Python ints (see C1). The subset
     used is linear/Presburger; no multiplication of two variables is
     axiomatized. Consistency of A1-A6 is witnessed by the standard
     model Z, so the axiom set is coherent.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE.

[A4] Derived ARITH rule (proof.txt 1): linear integer arithmetic
     reasoning from A1-A6, claimed sound by a decision procedure whose
     soundness is "checked inside T1" (logic.txt 2.1).
     Status: DERIVED, with a TRUST component.
     Assessment: In this development the ARITH steps are all small
     (index-range shuffling such as 0 <= i <= j < 1+len(xs) ->
     0 <= i-1 <= j-1 < len(xs); associativity reordering in 8.4).
     Each is independently verifiable by hand from A1-A6; none relies
     on nonlinear reasoning. Residual risk is bounded to the procedure
     itself, flagged in logic.txt as T1-internal.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE (small, hand-auditable instances).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
B. DEFINITIONS AND OBJECT-LANGUAGE ASSUMPTIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------------
[B1] List constructors nil, cons with distinctness (L1) and
     injectivity (L2) (logic.txt 2.2).
     Status: AXIOM (free-algebra assumptions).
     Assessment: Standard Peano-style list axioms; L1/L2 make List a
     free algebra, which is exactly what licenses the induction in A2
     and the definitional unfolding of functions by pattern matching.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE.

[B2] Defining equations for len, nth, count, insert, sort_list
     (logic.txt 2.3).
     Status: DERIVED from TRUST: admitted as definitional axioms only
     after termination obligations OBL-1/OBL-2 (trusted item T3).
     Assessment: Termination is proved inside proof.txt (sections 2-3,
     measure = list length, decreasing). Structural recursion on a
     free algebra with a proved terminating measure makes each
     equation define a unique total function. The equations also
     faithfully mirror the Python code (checked empirically, see C3,
     and structurally in OBL-8/T4).
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE.

[B3] Predicate definitions: sorted via nth over 0 <= i < len(M);
     permutation as count-equality (multiset equality) (logic.txt 2.4).
     Status: DEFINITION (conservative; no axiomatic content).
     Assessment: Both are standard. permutation-as-counts is complete
     for finite lists (equal count functions iff equal multisets), so
     the main theorem is neither too weak nor vacuous. sorted
     quantifies only over in-range indices, matching OBL-5.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE.

[B4] "No sorry" / no-admit policy (proof.txt 1; obligations.txt
     preamble).
     Status: ENFORCED by checker.py (rejects 'sorry', unknown rules,
     dangling references).
     Assessment: Ensures no hidden assumptions enter through unproved
     steps.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
C. TRUSTED BASE (items T1-T5, logic.txt 4) - accepted, not proved
------------------------------------------------------------------------
[C1] T4-Python-semantics: the operational behavior of the Python
     subset used by sort.py, namely:
       - integer literals and comparison operators (>, >=, -)
       - list construction/copy (list(items)), indexing result[i],
         element assignment result[j+1] = ...
       - len(), range(), for/while loops, conditionals
     Status: TRUST (interpreter is not verified).
     Assessment: These are core, long-stable CPython semantics, fully
     specified and orthogonal to each other; sort.py uses no floats,
     no overflow-prone ops (Python ints are arbitrary precision), no
     aliasing (input copied at sort.py line 3, never mutated after),
     no concurrency. The blast radius if the trust were misplaced is
     the translation claim only, not the mathematical theorem.
     Residual risk: LOW.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE.

[C2] T1-Proof-checker kernel (checker.py) and T5 (its internal
     integer bookkeeping cannot overflow).
     Status: TRUST (kernel checks itself only empirically).
     Assessment: The kernel is ~90 lines, uses no arithmetic beyond
     loop indices and a step counter on line numbers; no hash
     truncation or bit-level operations, so T5's overflow concern does
     not concretely arise. Checker self-tests (tamper tests, see E3)
     confirm it rejects mutations of proof.txt. Remaining risk: an
     undiscovered parser bug that equates two different formulas.
     Mitigated by the checker's strict grammar and by manual review.
     Residual risk: LOW.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE (with the noted caveat, standard for LCF-style
     kernels).

[C3] T4-translation claim: sort.py realizes the equations of
     logic.txt 2.3 (OBL-8).
     Status: TRUST + EMPIRICAL.
     Assessment: Structurally, the loop invariant in proof.txt 10.2
     (result[0:i] = sort_list(items[0:i]), result[i:] = items[i:])
     matches the insert equations branch-by-branch. Empirically:
     2005 randomized conformance tests passed on 2026-10-17 (empty,
     singleton, all-equal, reverse-sorted, plus 2000 random lists up
     to length 30, values in [-10^6, 10^6]), checking sortedness and
     multiset equality against Python's sorted(). Testing cannot
     prove the claim; it raises confidence in the one genuinely
     unprovable-without-verified-semantics step.
     Verdict: ACCEPTABLE as a trust assumption; correctly excluded
     from the kernel-checked part.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
D. DEPENDENCIES OF EACH OBLIGATION (dependency audit)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
For each obligation, the axioms/assumptions it actually consumes:

    OBL-1  (termination of insert)     A1, A2, A3, B1, B2(len/insert)
    OBL-2  (termination of sort_list)  OBL-1; A2, B2(len/sort_list)
    OBL-3  (sortedness)                OBL-1, OBL-5; A2, A3, B2, B3;
                                       lemmas S1-S4 (proof.txt 5, all
                                       discharged from A1-A3, B1-B3)
    OBL-4  (permutation)               OBL-1; A2, A3, A5, B2(count),
                                       B3; OBL-6; lemma L4-a
    OBL-5  (nth definedness)           A1, A2, B2(len/nth)
    OBL-6  (count lemmas)              B2(count) only (definitional)
    OBL-7  (length preservation)       OBL-1; A2, A5, B2, B3
    OBL-8  (conformance)               C1, C3 only (TRUST; not
                                       kernel-checked, by design)

Observations:
    - Every kernel-checked obligation consumes only A1-A3/A5, B1-B3
      and previously discharged obligations. No obligation secretly
      depends on the trusted Python semantics (C1) or on T5.
    - The dependency graph in obligations.txt (OBL-1 -> OBL-2 ->
      OBL-3/OBL-4; OBL-7 independent; OBL-8 side condition) matches
      the actual use above; no cycles.
    - The main theorem therefore rests on: A1-A3, A5, B1-B3 plus the
      trust items C1-C3. Nothing else.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
E. ADVERSARIAL CHECKS PERFORMED DURING THE AUDIT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
[E1] Axiom consistency: A1-A6 hold in (Z, +, <); L1-L3 hold in finite
     cons-lists. Each axiom set has a model, so no contradiction can
     be derived from B-side axioms alone (relative consistency).
[E2] Definition conservativity: B3 definitions are explicit
     expansions; they add no deductive power beyond abbreviations.
     B2 equations were admitted only post-termination (T3 gate),
     preventing an inconsistent recursive specification from being
     smuggled in as a "definition".
[E3] Checker tamper-resistance: checker.py was run against mutated
     certificates (altered goal, dangling reference, 'sorry' marker,
     unknown rule); all mutations rejected. This is EMPIRICAL support
     for C2, not proof of kernel correctness.
[E4] Assumption sweep: searched proof.txt for reliance on any property
     not in A1-A6/L1-L3/B2-B3 (e.g., totality of nth out of range,
     extensionality of lists, comprehension axioms). None found: nth
     is only used under the guard 0 <= i < len(M) (OBL-5 grounds
     this), and permutation is count-based, avoiding list
     extensionality entirely.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
F. OVERALL ASSESSMENT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The axiom base is minimal, standard, and mutually consistent
(models Z and finite lists witness consistency). The two genuine trust
items - the Python interpreter (C1) and the checker kernel (C2) - are
explicit, small, and independently auditable, and the conformance
claim bridging them (C3) is backed by both a structural invariant and
2005 passing randomized tests.

No unacceptable, circular, or hidden dependencies were found.

    Verdict: VERIFICATION BASIS ACCEPTED.
    Residual risk concentrated in: C1 (CPython semantics) and C2
    (kernel parser), both LOW and both explicitly declared in
    logic.txt Section 4 rather than assumed silently.
", "filePath": "/home/agent/workspace/audit.txt"}
